subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the black-armored cloaked warrior in <Picture 1>, carrying one long straight sword in the right hand.

<Subject 2> is the enormous rock-bodied monster in <Picture 1>, with a massive stone torso, heavy segmented stone arms, giant fists, and no weapon.

<Subject 3> is the dark gothic cathedral in <Picture 1>, featuring towering stone columns, red and blue stained-glass light, stone-tile flooring, fallen rubble, drifting dust, and breakable masonry.

summary:

[reference generation] An eight-second cinematic close-quarters fight between <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> inside <Subject 3>. The warrior uses side entries, rolls, low slides, column cover, and precise sword strikes into existing rock seams to evade the monster’s crushing stone-arm attacks.

detailed_description:

The target video is a dark, high-end fantasy action sequence with grounded scale, readable attack lines, realistic debris behavior, and intense red-blue cathedral lighting. There are no additional characters, weapons, dialogue, or supernatural effects.

[Shot 1] <Subject 2>, the enormous stone monster, sweeps a near-side stone arm horizontally across <Subject 3>, its fist driving fragments and dust ahead of it. <Subject 1>, the black-armored warrior with a single right-hand straight sword, slides outside the crushing line beneath the forearm. During the slide, the sword rises into a narrow seam at the monster’s wrist; sparks and stone chips burst as the arm is forced slightly upward. <Subject 1> continues directly toward the monster’s leg side. The camera races low across the tiles, passing beneath the stone arm while keeping the fist trajectory, sliding body, and sword contact in one clear line.

[Shot 2] At 00:02.000, <Subject 2> converts the redirected arm into a downward fist strike. The fist smashes the tiles behind <Subject 1>, throwing broken stone and dust forward. <Subject 1> rolls ahead of the impact, rises from one knee, cuts along the new floor crack, and drives the sword briefly into a gap between stone plates at the monster’s forward leg before pulling it free. The monster shifts weight backward and crushes more tiles under one foot. The camera jolts from the floor impact, then swings into a lateral pursuit of the warrior’s route around the giant’s side.

[Shot 3] At 00:04.000, <Subject 2> turns and drives the other fist down to close the narrow lane between its body and a tall column. <Subject 1> runs tight along the inner side of the column as the fist grazes the stone surface, showering fragments downward. The warrior lowers beneath the debris and cuts upward across a cracked edge of the monster’s forearm. The blade recoil pushes <Subject 1> back one step while a shallow new fracture opens; the monster’s arm sweeps onward and clips a damaged column, sending masonry down. The camera follows behind the warrior’s shoulder, tilts with the fist impact, then threads through the falling rubble.

[Shot 4] At 00:06.000, the unstable forearm presses down again. <Subject 1> jumps left of the descending path, plants a boot on a newly fallen stone, and redirects through the monster’s side. Mid-turn, the straight sword cuts into the existing crack across the back of the stone hand. <Subject 1> lands, withdraws the blade, and slides around the monster’s flank as the giant hand crushes into the floor. Dust rolls outward from the impact and the warrior enters it with the sword still pointed forward for the next close entry. The camera skims beside the stone hand and follows the warrior into the dust, with falling rubble, cloak movement, and the advancing sword line active in the final frame.

overall_soundscape:

Deep air pressure from sweeping stone arms, armor and boots scraping over tile, a sword grinding against rock, massive fists breaking stone flooring, column fragments collapsing, dust and rubble falling, and the enclosed cathedral echo. No dialogue, narration, captions, or visible text.

non_diegetic_music:

Heavy war drums, low brass pressure tones, aggressive bowed strings, and rising percussion that intensifies with every near miss and stone impact.
